system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: The periodic HTTPS activity is attributable to C:\Program Files\PixelForge\pfupdater.exe: the process was observed running on WS-LMARTINS-01, and its network connection to the explicit proxy is recorded at the same time.

Proxy records identify the destination as updates.pixelforge-suite.com, which matches the supplied approved PixelForge update service. Successful tunnels are recorded at 13:41, 13:46, 13:50, and 14:05 UTC, with attempts around 13:35, 13:55, and 14:01 UTC; the intervals are roughly five minutes.

The proxy records show a mix of authentication-required and denied attempts as well as successful tunnels; this pattern is consistent with updater checks encountering proxy access outcomes, rather than evidence of a successful connection to an unapproved service.

Other recorded network activity in the interval includes internal Kerberos, LDAP, and SMB traffic involving the workstation and DC-NWD-01. The available records show computer-account authentication for some SMB sessions but do not establish a connection between that activity and the periodic proxy traffic.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records provide CONNECT destination, outcome, and tunnel byte counts, but do not expose the encrypted HTTPS contents or establish what was exchanged inside successful tunnels.
The supplied process and network records do not include a binary hash or signature-validation result for pfupdater.exe.
The SMB records are connection summaries and do not identify the accessed share or files.
claims_not_established: The contents or precise purpose of data exchanged in the successful HTTPS tunnels.
Whether pfupdater.exe on disk was authentic and unmodified.
The precise purpose of the separate internal SMB and LDAP activity.
